::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal" icon="false" title="Purpose"}
Use this guide with the Week 12 lecture, readings, videos, and sampling lab. It
connects sampling decisions, sources of survey error, and question design to
the claims a researcher can responsibly make.

Keep the completed guide as a reference for Project 2 and the survey research
quiz.
:::

## Objectives

- distinguish populations, sampling frames, samples, and response pools;
- compare probability and nonprobability sampling methods;
- distinguish randomness, representativeness, sampling error, and bias;
- identify common sources of survey error;
- evaluate question wording and response options; and
- state conclusions that fit the sampling and data-collection process.

## Resources

- [Week 12 slides](week_12.qmd)
- [Bias and Error in Survey Research](readings/bias-error-survey-research.qmd)
- [Survey Design chapter from *Data and Design*](https://trinachi.github.io/data-design-builds/ch03.html)
- the Pew Research Center Methods 101 videos in Canvas

## 1) Map the survey process

Complete each definition for the class survey or another survey discussed in
class.

| Term | Definition | Example from the survey |
|---|---|---|
| Target population | The complete group the researcher wants to understand |  |
| Sampling frame | The people who had a realistic chance to be selected or invited |  |
| Sample | The people selected or invited from the frame |  |
| Response pool | The people who supplied usable responses |  |
| Observational unit | What one row of the resulting dataset represents |  |

Why might the response pool differ from the intended sample?

## 7) Evaluate a survey claim

Choose one published survey result or one result from the class survey.

1. State the claim and intended population.
2. Describe the sampling frame, selection method, and response pool.
3. Identify one possible source of random error and one possible source of
   systematic bias.
4. Identify one question-design or mode concern.
5. Rewrite the conclusion so it does not claim more than the design supports.

## Completion checklist

- [ ] I distinguished the population, frame, sample, and response pool.
- [ ] I compared probability and nonprobability sampling methods.
- [ ] I separated random sampling error from systematic bias.
- [ ] I diagnosed question-wording and response-option problems.
- [ ] I evaluated a survey conclusion using its design and limitations.
